selectedMessages.text: for internet toggle to isolate env it could be an env selection instead of a toggle internet onoff where the no internet env is the same evrything (storage and data and session and history? can they share the same and multi read write?) and difference only for a seperate comptute and network? is this design better or more efficient aand optimized?

Selected proposal: The optimized design is:

Keep a small warm offline pool and online pool, rather than creating a new pod for every request.
Route each login/session to exactly one pool.
Keep that session pinned to the selected environment.
Store durable history centrally.
Permit only one active writer for each session or workspace.
Use an approved staging folder to move files between environments.
Require a new session, or an explicit controlled handover, when switching environments.
Keep LiteLLM and the four-GPU model shared, so no additional GPU copy is required.
This provides concurrent use: offline and online users can work simultaneously, and multiple short model requests can still run concurrently. The additional cost is mainly lightweight CPU/RAM pods and storage—not another GPU model.
I recommend renaming the UI control from Internet Off/On to Working environment: Secure/Internal or Internet, because selecting it routes the user to a different protected execution environment rather than merely changing a browser preference.
User response: so implement. the sharing work space was because we need the internet env to install required library for the no internet env

The shared CIFS volume ignored the ownership change and kept the directories as `root:root`. I’m testing the future non-root identity against the exact subpath now; if it cannot write, I’ll adjust the storage boundary rather than leaving a manifest that only looks secure.

The exact CIFS write test failed for non-root, so I replaced the shared folders with separate local Kubernetes volumes for authentication, package intake, approved packages and each pool token. This prevents cross-environment reads and supports non-root ownership. I’m now verifying that design against the live storage driver before committing it.

A second live boundary check matters: the protected CIFS workspace is also root-owned, so a non-root Secure pod could not write it. I’m moving the future Secure workspace to its own local volume and adding a suspended migration job that copies existing projects and authentication data during controlled rollout. This keeps the current Production data untouched until cutover.

A migration gap was found before cutover: project files were copied exactly, but the legacy 3.5 GB DSH session/history store was excluded, leaving the Secure candidate empty. I will not switch ingress in that state. I’m updating the migration to copy the session store into Secure state, then I’ll verify its counts and sizes and retest persistence.

The public endpoint is now verified after cutover: TLS login loaded, Secure is the default, registration and password change worked, the old password was rejected, both environment choices pinned to the correct backend, both backends rendered DSH, and logout cleared the session. The temporary test account was removed. The old main `dsh` deployment is scaled to zero for rollback; DSH2 and DSH3 were not changed.

I’m continuing with the remaining safety item: read back the live LiteLLM and model limits, then apply the already tested 128K guardrail with the saved rollback if the live objects match the prepared configuration.
